concerns.text: FR-012 (directory structure: code/, data/raw/, ... state/projects/) cites only '(Evidence for verification tasks)' and names no user story; no story's scope covers repository scaffolding. Re-anchor it to a story (e.g. US-1's reproducible-foundation scope) or remove it from this spec.
FR-013 (state/setup_log.txt with recursive listing) is anchored only to '(Evidence for verification tasks)'; no user story asks for a setup log. Re-anchor or remove.
FR-014 (code/.ruff.toml strict linting + CI ruff step) has no story anchor; linting/CI configuration is not requested by US-1/2/3. Re-anchor (e.g. to US-2's reproducibility rationale) or remove.
FR-015 (pytest.ini with seed pinning + tests/conftest.py) cites only '(Evidence for verification tasks)'; no user story covers test configuration. Re-anchor or remove.

FR-001 says if pathway labels are missing the system MUST apply a rule-based synthetic label distribution; FR-008 says if labels are missing it MUST flag the record for manual curation or exclusion. Two FRs mandate different handling of the identical condition (missing labels) without reconciling when each applies. US-1 scenario 4 allows either ('synthetic label distribution or flags the record'), so the FRs themselves conflict.

FR-010 requires an external validation set of ≥30 experimentally verified polymer degradation records, but FR-011 forbids any dataset other than NIST Chemistry WebBook and Materials Project — the same sources FR-001 says lack pathway labels (hence synthetic labeling). The spec never states where experimentally verified records come from; as written the two FRs cannot both be satisfied.

concerns.location: spec.md:FR-004, FR-019, US-2 scenario 3 vs constitution.md Principle VII
concerns.text: The spec mandates augmentation via edge dropout and subgraph sampling (FR-004, FR-019, US-2.3), while the project constitution Principle VII mandates 'bond rotation and atom masking'. The augmentation method is named inconsistently between the spec and its own constitution; one must be reconciled to the other.

FR-006 mandates a permutation test (≥1000 permutations) as the significance test, relegating χ² to 'categorical count tables that satisfy its assumptions'. Constitution Principle VI states model predictions 'MUST be validated using the χ² statistical test at α=0.05'. The primary statistical test is contradictory between spec and constitution.

SC-004 ties the <150-instance condition to a 'power-analysis warning (G*Power simulation, power ≥0.8)', while FR-009 and the Edge Cases section tie the same condition to switching to leave-one-out validation. Not contradictory, but the two responses to the same threshold are never cross-referenced, leaving it unclear whether both fire. Add a cross-reference for a single consistent small-sample policy.

FR-010 demands an external validation set of ≥30 experimentally verified polymer degradation records, but FR-011 restricts data sources to NIST WebBook and Materials Project, and FR-001/US-1 acknowledge pathway labels may be missing (requiring synthetic labels). If the permitted sources lack ≥30 experimentally verified labeled records, this input is unreachable and the criterion cannot be evaluated. Specify the source of the external set or a documented fallback (e.g., manual curation from literature with citations) so the acceptance input is reachable.

FR-001 requires synthetic class frequencies to 'match literature-reported proportions within a 10 % tolerance' but names no literature reference for those proportions. Without a citable reference (specific paper(s) or reported distribution), the 10 % comparison has no verifiable baseline. Name the reference the frequencies are checked against.

The fallback verification path 'if labels are synthetic, via literature-based motif validation' is not a defined procedure — no steps, reference, or pass/fail rule are given, so an implementer cannot know when it is satisfied. Specify the validation procedure (e.g., which literature source and what comparison counts as a pass).

SC-008 defines the measurement (percentage of low-confidence predictions correctly flagged) but states no target threshold or pass condition, so it is not decidable met-or-not. Add a target (e.g., 100 % of softmax < 0.6 predictions carry the flag) or state the acceptance rule.

Idea and constitution (Principle VI) mandate a χ² statistical test at α=0.05 comparing model predictions to a random-assignment baseline. The spec replaces this with a permutation test ('χ² may be used only for categorical count tables'). This silently redefines the mandated validation method; either restore χ² as the primary test or explicitly reconcile with the constitution's non-negotiable requirement.

Idea methodology and constitution Principle VII specify augmentation via 'bond rotation and atom masking' (~2×, 30-min limit). The spec substitutes 'edge dropout and subgraph sampling' without justification. This is drift from both the source idea and the constitution; restore the mandated augmentation methods or document why the substitution is equivalent.

The idea's methodology includes 'Generate visualization of top 5 degradation pathways with their associated structural motifs using networkx'. The spec's report requirements (FR-007, SC-012) cover only a JSON report; the visualization deliverable is dropped. Either add it or state it is out of scope.

Circular label construction: FR-001 generates synthetic labels by rules keyed to motifs ('ester → hydrolysis, aromatic → photolysis'). The GNN is then trained to predict those labels from the same motifs, so SC-001's macro-F1 ≥ 0.70 on synthetic labels and SC-005's finding that IG highlights ester bonds for hydrolysis are true BY CONSTRUCTION, not empirical findings. The 'literature-based motif validation' fallback in SC-005 validates the labeling rule against itself.

SC-005 requires IG to identify ester linkages as top features for ≥90% of hydrolysis cases. When labels are synthetic (ester→hydrolysis), this cannot fail — the model only needs to learn the injected rule. The 'null distribution of shuffled motifs' with a two-tailed t-test does not break this circularity; the null comparison is against the same rule-generated data.

FR-010's external validation set of ≥30 'experimentally verified' records is the only non-circular evidence, but no source for such records is named, and the spec's own literature-gap analysis states no public dataset linking SMILES + conditions + observed pathways exists. If the external set cannot be assembled, SC-001's ≥0.70 on it is unachievable; the spec needs a named, verifiable source or a fallback that halts claims of empirical structure-mechanism findings.

Constitution VI mandates χ² validation at α=0.05; FR-006 replaces this with a permutation test, allowing χ² 'only for categorical count tables.' The permutation test is statistically preferable, but the spec silently deviates from a NON-NEGOTIABLE-adjacent constitutional principle without noting or justifying the amendment — this should be reconciled explicitly.

A two-tailed t-test against a permutation/shuffled-motif null distribution is the wrong estimator: permutation nulls yield an empirical p-value directly (as FR-006 correctly specifies for US-3). Applying a t-test to attribution scores across non-independent per-atom scores within the same molecule violates independence assumptions. Use the empirical permutation p-value consistently.

new_concerns.text: Circular validation remains: SC-005 still requires Integrated Gradients to identify ester linkages as top features for ≥90 % of hydrolysis cases. When synthetic labels (ester → hydrolysis) are used, the model can trivially satisfy this by learning the rule, so the claim is still true by construction. Adding FR‑021 ablation does not remove the original requirement; the spec must either (a) drop the synthetic‑label‑only IG requirement, or (b) require the IG motif validation exclusively on the external experimentally‑verified validation set.

The same circularity applies to the Integrated Gradients motif relevance claim. Even with FR‑021, SC‑005 still predicates on synthetic labeling and therefore cannot fail. The specification must decouple the IG evaluation from the rule‑based synthetic labels, e.g., by mandating IG assessment only on records with experimentally verified pathways.
